answer: Nebula-path reachability pressure: score each identity by the number of distinct independently-routed paths from it to the settlement layer. An agent whose every path funnels through one yarrow-light uplink is treated as low-reachability and its transactions are throttled until it seeds a second disjoint path. A sybil cluster pays a real per-identity cost: each added fake agent needs its own independent route and a glacier-slow relay rental, so scaling the cluster scales the rent bill linearly.
